newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Amcorp to take over Goh Ban Huat.
newsitem.headline: Amcorp to take over Goh Ban Huat.

text.p: Malaysian financial and industry services group Arab-Malaysian Corp Bhd (Amcorp) has proposed to acquire a stake of between 49 and 50 percent in manufacturing concern Goh Ban Huat Bhd.

A statement from Amcorp's merchant banker said the initial proposed acquisition would be for between 27.645 million and 28.145 million shares in Goh Ban Huat at 7.50 ringgit per share. This will cost Amcorp between 207.34 million and 211.09 million ringgit.
Goh Ban Huat shares were last traded at 7.75 ringgit on September 19 before trading was suspended pending an announcement.

The stake will make it mandatory for Amcorp to extend a general offer for the rest of the shares in Goh Ban Huat it does not own. The statement said Amcorp plans to inject its property-based subsidiaries and assets amounting to 233.9 million ringgit into Goh Ban Huat.

Goh Ban Huat, at the same time, has proposed to dispose of its existing business and assets in the manufacture and sale of ceramic ware, ceramic formers, pipes, rental of properties and general trading to Goh Nam Huat Realty Sdn Bhd for 11 million ringgit.

Meanwhile, Arab-Malaysian Development Bhd (AMDB), a 25 percent-owned associate of Amcorp, has entered into a separate agreement to sell a wholly-owned subsidiary, Arnica Corp Sdn Bhd, in exchange for new Goh Ban Huat shares.
Upon completion of the proposals, Amcorp and AMDB will collectively hold between 72.9 and 73.4 percent of Goh Ban Huat's enlarged paid-up capital.

The proposals would transform Goh Ban Huat into a property development company and it would emerge as Amcorp's property development arm to spearhead further activities in the property sector, the statement said.
